caseIds: P1 — the LIVE default: nothing that is not strictly a retest can be refused
P2 — a retest UNDER the cap is allowed and carries no scope
P3 — the per-student boundary: N-1 allowed, N refused
P4 — the GLOBAL cap trips independently of the per-student cap
P5 — asymmetric failure semantics: live fails OPEN, retest fails CLOSED
P6 — counterAt: the KST window rollover IS the reset (no sweeper)
P7 — nextCounter writes the frozen {count, windowStart} shape
P8 — limits are CONFIG with DEFAULTS; the refusal shape is the frozen idiom
P9 — ONE day law: the window key IS completion.js's kstDateString
M-COUNT — create: a fresh claim grades, counts once, and stamps aiCallCount
M-IDEMP — set-merge/return_cached: a retried claim of an ALREADY-COUNTED job does NOT double-count
M-IDEMP-DELETED — delete-then-recreate SEQUENCE: a re-claim after deletion is a REAL new call
M-INPROGRESS — set-overwrite/live lease: no grader, no count
M-TAKEOVER — update: an EXPIRED lease re-grades, so it counts again (aiCallCount 1→2)
M-THIRD-PARTY — as a third party: a foreign job throws BEFORE any meter read or write
M-TEACHER — as a teacher: the same fence, the same zero-count outcome
M-SOLE-WRITER — batch: the ONLY writer of ai_metering/* is this transaction
M-RETEST-UNDER — a rerun under the cap grades and counts
M-RETEST-BOUNDARY — the per-student cap trips at the boundary, with ZERO writes on refusal
M-LIVE-OVERCAP — ★ THE OUTAGE CASE: the SAME over-cap state does NOT refuse a LIVE test
M-GLOBAL — the global cap refuses a retest while the student is at zero
M-ROLLOVER — a KST day boundary resets the window by construction
M-NO-DISCRIMINATOR — a missing discriminator reads as LIVE and is allowed
M-CONFIG-UNREADABLE — config outage: live proceeds (fail-OPEN), retest refuses (fail-CLOSED)
M-METER-READ-THROWS — a counter read failure never fails a live claim
M-LIVE-TXN-GLOBAL-FREE — ★ THE CONTENTION LAW: a LIVE claim never touches _global in its txn
M-DEFERRED-WINDOW — the deferred writer rolls the KST window without losing counts
M-DEFERRED-FAILURE — a failed global increment never fails or delays the grade
M-REBUILD-FAITHFUL — the un-mutated rebuild matches the real export before any mutant is judged
